architecture.mechanism: Stability of complex systems is governed by adherence to fundamental universal invariants; deviation from these constraints destabilizes the system, so the 1-2 shift harshness is treated as a control variable drifting outside its invariant bounds (clutch slip/shaft-speed synchronization during the handoff) rather than a purely mechanical defect.
architecture.intervention: Recalibrate the transmission control module so the 1-2 shift executes closed-loop pressure ramping that holds clutch slip rate and output-shaft speed error within the identified invariant envelope (adaptive learning of the invariant bounds per fluid temperature and load), instead of relying on the open-loop shift map.
architecture.expected_effect: The first-to-second handoff converges to the stable invariant trajectory, eliminating the intermittent harsh shift while keeping clutch apply within factory thermal and wear limits, so durability is not degraded.
architecture.falsification_test: Instrument a vehicle with pressure, shaft-speed, jerk (m/s³) and clutch temperature sensors; log 100+ standstill-to-second-gear events across cold/hot fluid and varying loads before and after the recalibration; the fix is falsified if peak jerk or clutch energy per shift is not reduced to within the invariant band, or if clutch temperature/wear indicators worsen.
